question: Immigration will continue to be one of the major topics of public debate in the run-up to the European elections. The topic of immigration has influenced decisions such as Austria voting against Romania’s accession to the Schengen area. This is a reflection of Europe’s broader concerns about illegal immigration and the need for efficient management at the EU’s external borders, where Romania plays a key role. 1.
Given its strategic position on the EU’s external border, how will the Commission help Romania limit illegal immigration while also ensuring the humane treatment of asylum seekers?
In the context of the continuing efforts to promote social cohesion, what is the Commission doing to address the challenges of the integration and social inclusion of refugees and migrants?
answer: 1. As demonstrated inter alia through the Schengen evaluation process (1), Romania has a high-quality border management system in place including efficient border surveillance, border checks and solid international cooperation.

On 3 March 2024, the Commission launched together with Romania and Bulgaria two cooperation frameworks to further strengthen the joint European efforts to protect the EU external borders and effectively address migration challenges in full compliance with fundamental rights (2).

Finally, the Commission also launched a new funding specific action of EUR 85 million to enhance national capabilities at the EU external borders, to which Romania was invited to apply (3). 2. National governments are primarily responsible for integration policies, while the EU supports Member States through funding, developing guidance and fostering partnerships.
The Commission’s action plan on Integration and Inclusion 20212027 (4) puts forward a comprehensive policy framework and sets out over 60 actions.

Integration is a long-term crosscutting process, supported through the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (tailor-made early horizontal measures), the European Social Fund Plus (labour market integration and social inclusion of migrants), the European Regional Development Fund (inclusion through infrastructure, equipment and access to services in education, employment, housing, social, health and childcare).
The technical support instrument is also available to support integration policies.
